title: company.json
description: The seller fingerprint. Answers exactly one question: who is this company? Written by gtme-company, read by every downstream stage. Market claims belong in market-pain.json; interpretations and raw hooks belong in seller-research.json.

positioning_history.description: How the company has described itself over time. Empty prior/removed_claims means the Wayback pass ran and found no change - a different claim from not looking, so say where you looked in decisions.md.

removed_claims.description: Claims the company took down. The highest-signal part of this field and the one gtme-write must never reinstate: a dropped logo or a softened metric is the company telling you what it could not defend.

removed_between.description: Window the removal is bounded to, e.g. 2026-03/2026-07.

go_to_market.description: How the company sells today. Read by gtme-offer (an offer designed against a sales-led motion is a different object from one designed against self-serve) and gtme-icp (no self-serve narrows which segments are reachable at all).

entry_point.description: What a buyer actually clicks and where it lands, e.g. 'book-a-demo form to founder inbox'.

founders.description: Founders only. First hires and other staff go in team.members.

headcount_confirmed.description: People actually found and named. null only if the org could not be enumerated at all.

headcount_claimed.description: What the company says. Differs from confirmed more often than not; that gap is a finding, not an error.

members.description: Every publicly findable non-founder. The review question fails on a missing person.

unidentified.description: Roles claimed to exist but not resolvable to a person. Names the hole instead of hiding it.

platform.description: The substrate products run on. A company may operate several (AWS and the retail marketplace are two). null or empty is correct for a single-product company - never pad this to look complete.

properties.description: Only what holds true across ALL products on this platform.

products.description: A sellable thing a buyer adopts on its own. A seller with no product cannot be sold.

metrics.description: Attach a number at the level its SOURCE attaches it. A metric the site pins to one loop does not decorate the flagship claim.

window.description: The explicit time window the result was measured over. null means the source did not state one - which is itself a caveat gtme-write must honor.

achievements.description: Traction, metrics, press, awards - evidence the PRODUCT works. Every entry cited.

credibility.description: Evidence the COMPANY is legitimate - institutions vouching, not customer outcomes. Kept separate from achievements because this is where puffery lives, and gtme-write must be able to treat a founder-claimed ranking differently from a measured customer result.

verification.description: Per-item, not per-field. A founder_claimed award quoted as fact in outreach is a reputation risk. disproven is stronger than unfindable: the claim was checked and is false, so gtme-write must never restate it - a distinction that matters most when the buyer's own job is detecting false claims.

rounds.description: Every publicly disclosed financing round, oldest first, with its terms. One entry per round from pre-seed through whatever the latest is - there is no cap, Series M is a legal value. Empty array means the search was run and no round is public; say where you looked in decisions.md, because an empty list and an unsearched one must not read the same.

investors.description: The union of everyone on the cap table, across all rounds plus anyone whose round is unknown. Stays even when rounds is fully populated: angels named on a site with no round attached have nowhere else to live.

verification.description: Same evidence classes as rounds[], because this list summarizes them. secondhand = a tracker lists them and nothing primary confirms it.

certifications.description: Empty means searched and none published.

via.description: Auditor or compliance vendor, when findable.

regulatory_vocabulary.description: Whether the company's own public material speaks the buyer's regulatory language. This is a FACT about their copy. What it implies about which segments are reachable is an inference and belongs in icp.json, not here.

warm_universe.description: Everyone the seller already knows who touches the ICP. Required in full - the pipeline cannot choose to skip warm outreach if it never asked who is warm.

founder_orbit.description: Read by gtme-score for warmth points. ONLY places a founder actually worked or studied. An angel check from a company is not a relationship with everyone who worked there; investors here manufacture warmth that does not exist.

exhausted.description: false until warm outreach has actually been run or explicitly waived at a gate. gtme-offer's warm-first plan reads this.

competitors.description: Part of the fingerprint - who a company displaces defines it. Bare names are useless downstream; these are scrape targets for competitor-engagement signals.

oneOf.description: Legal only when domain is null - there was nothing to fetch.

identityCheck.description: Proof the domain was FETCHED, not inferred from the name. A name-match is not enough: two unrelated companies can share a name (a run shipped a fraud-AML competitor at an FX-hedging startup's domain, because both are called Bretton). So the check is a verbatim line of the served page describing what it SELLS - which a human or a later agent can compare against `relation` and see the mismatch. Null domain means null identity.

pulled.description: Date the domain was actually fetched.

says.description: Verbatim from the served page: what this company sells and to whom. Not a summary you wrote, and not the company name alone.

cites.description: Numbered references into this folder's provenance.md.

oneOf.description: Looked for it, found nothing. Distinct from the field being absent.

roundDate.description: ISO, truncated to the precision the source actually gives: 2025, 2025-03, or 2025-03-14. null = the round is public but this date isn't. Never widen a month into a day you inferred.

round.description: One financing round and its publicly disclosed terms. Every term field is nullable because most rounds disclose some and not others - null means searched and not public, which is a different claim from the round not existing.

stage.description: As the source names it: pre-seed, seed, seed extension, bridge, Series A, Series B ... Series M. Do not normalize - a seed extension collapsed into 'seed' loses the fact that they went back to the same well.

size.description: Amount raised, with currency and full figure: "$1,000,000". null = round disclosed, size not.

date_announced.description: When it was made public. Often months after close, and the gap is itself a signal.

valuation.description: With pre or post stated: "$10M post". Only if a source states it - never back-compute it from size and equity.

equity.description: Percent of the company sold, e.g. "10%". Only if a source states it; a figure you divided out of size and valuation is a derivation, not a disclosed term.

instrument.description: SAFE, priced equity, convertible note, venture debt. Decides whether valuation and equity are even meaningful for this round.

investors.description: Who was in THIS round. Every name here must also appear in stage.investors, which stays the union across all rounds and carries the per-investor verification.

role.description: unknown is honest when the announcement names investors without saying who led.

verification.description: verified = read on a primary filing, the company's own announcement, or first-party press. secondhand = a tracker (Crunchbase, PitchBook, Tracxn) with no primary behind it - those carry standard-deal placeholders and stale amounts constantly.

pain.description: The pain this capability kills, written the way the BUYER ranks it. Vendor framing fails the skeptical-buyer critic.

urgency.description: nice_to_have is allowed but is a flag: sharpen it from evidence or cut the capability.

note.description: One factual clause, e.g. last posted 2024-03.

bio.description: Career arc in 2-3 sentences, verified facts only. Unverified claims stay in seller-research.json.

employer_history.description: Where they worked before. Feeds founder_orbit for founders.

relationships.description: Named people or communities that constitute a warm path.
